title: Constrained derivative-free MAP returns its starting point (constant grand-mean vector) and reports 'constrained optimum reached' whenever the Powell optimum is a hair infeasible on several tied constraints (increasing d>=10 with multiple pooled blocks, convex d>=7, concave d>=6)
reproduction: cd <review-root>/reviews-081/pass-04 && <review-root>/candidate-081/venv/bin/python repro_F01.py   # self-contained: builds DiagGaussian(d, mean=free(d,name='v'), var=fixed) on 200 rows/column with column means (a) RandomState(101).permutation(10)*0.3 and constraints=[increasing(v)], (b) 0,2,1,3,4,...,9 and constraints=[convex(v)], fits how='map', rng=RandomState(1), prints fit vs hand PAV / SLSQP convex-regression target and the NLL gap. Broader sweep: attackA_isotonic.py (d=1..20) and attackD_sweep.py (d=6..15, random permutations at d=10,20). Mechanism trace: repro_convex10.py (wraps scipy.optimize.minimize to print every Powell/Nelder-Mead call).
expected: The constrained MAP = isotonic (PAV) / convex-regression projection of the column means, e.g. increasing d=10 -> [1.032 x3, 1.168, 1.534 x6]; convex d=10 -> [0.456, 1.095, 1.734, 2.787, ..., 9.109]; or an exception if the optimizer cannot get there.
observed: increasing d=10: fitted mean [1.347]*10 (= grand mean = start u0), max|err| 0.315, 221 nats worse than PAV. convex d=10: [4.492]*9+[4.497], max|err| 4.61, 34,222 nats worse. Same for increasing d=20 random perms (8,708 / 3,613 nats), convex d=7,8,12,15,20 (incl. d=20 interior case where the constraint is inactive: returns constant 19.01 vs target 0.03..38.0), concave d=6..15. Fit returns normally, explain_fit route='map', no warning. Trace: the Powell ramp converges to within 0.02 of the target, then _repair_feasibility's normals step fails on overlapping tied constraints, its segment-to-anchor fallback returns t=1 (the anchor u0 lies ON the shape-constraint boundary so every t<1 stays infeasible), Nelder-Mead polish from u0 cannot move against the wall, and _derivative_free_constrained returns (u0, ..., True, 'constrained optimum reached').
notes: This is the defect class the 0.8.1 CHANGELOG entry 'Constrained derivative-free MAP fits ... no longer ... report convergence at a nearly constant vector far from the constrained optimum' claims fixed; the fix holds for the tutorial's 5-D data (verified: executed tutorial prints [0.01 1.44 1.44 3.06 3.99]) and low d, and fails for the notebooks' own recipe at >=8-10 positions with more than one pooled block. d=1,2,5 all constraints, d=10/20 increasing with one adjacent swap, and lipschitz d=6..15 are correct. A check that the repaired/polished point is no worse than the ramp's final iterate would catch every case.

title: Constrained MAP path never checks Powell convergence: max_iter=1 returns a wrong point as a success while the unconstrained path raises
reproduction: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import DiagGaussian, free, increasing, Normal; r=np.random.RandomState(0); X=np.stack([r.normal(l,0.5,300) for l in [0,2,1,3,4]],axis=1).tolist(); v=free(5,name='v'); f=DiagGaussian(5,mean=v,var=np.full(5,.25)).fit(X,how='map',constraints=[increasing(v)],max_iter=1,rng=np.random.RandomState(0)); print(np.round(f.params['mean'],3)); Normal(Normal(0,10,name='mu'),free).fit(list(r.normal(5,2,400)),how='map',max_iter=1)"   (see also attackB.log 'max_iter=1 (kw)', attackE 'constrained map max_iter=1')
expected: Either a RuntimeError naming max_iter (as the unconstrained L-BFGS and no-torch Nelder-Mead paths raise) or a non-success flag; the PAV answer is [0.014, 1.44, 1.44, 3.059, 3.992].
observed: Constrained call returns [0.014, 1.191, 1.191, 3.059, 3.992] with no error or warning; the unconstrained call raises 'RuntimeError: MAP optimization failed: STOP: TOTAL NO. OF ITERATIONS REACHED LIMIT'.
notes: Combined with P04-F01, the 'success' flag on the constrained path carries no information; the CHANGELOG's 'Failure messages name max_iter' is moot when budget exhaustion is not detected.

title: Constrained MAP whose optimum is a fully-tied corner (all coordinates pooled) stops 0.005-0.03 short of the pooled mean (2-3 standard errors, up to ~3 nats)
surface: mixle.ppl.inference._derivative_free_constrained: Nelder-Mead polish against the 1e18 wall from a point where every constraint is active
reproduction: cd <review-root>/reviews-081/pass-04 && <venv>/bin/python repro_decreasing5.py   # d=5, decreasing(v) on data with increasing column means 0,2,4,6,8 (sd 0.5, n=200/col, var fixed 0.25); optimum is the constant grand-mean vector. attackA.log rows scenario='interior', constraint='decreasing' for d=5 and d=10.
expected: Constant vector at the grand mean to ~1e-6 (tol=1e-8 requested), e.g. 3.9774 / 4.0194 / 3.9761 for seeds 0/1/2; 9.0016 for d=10.
observed: 3.9829 / 4.0311 / 3.9813 (errors 0.0055-0.0117, 0.06-0.27 nats); d=10: 9.0301 vs 9.0016 (err 0.0285, ~3.3 nats, pooled-mean SE 0.011). Trace: the weight-1e9 Powell iterate is already off by this amount; the polish returns its start because every simplex vertex u+1e-3*e_k (k>=1) breaks a tie and hits the wall.
notes: Small in absolute terms but systematic and growing with d, at exactly the configuration the constraint exists for.

title: how='hmc' with an active hard constraint returns a degenerate 'posterior' (acceptance 0.0, all draws equal to the projected start, std 0) with no error; vector models raise a non-finite-gradient ValueError
reproduction: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Normal, free; dd=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(5,2,400)); mu=Normal(0,10,name='mu'); f=Normal(mu,free).fit(dd,how='hmc',draws=2000,burn=500,constraints=[mu>6],rng=np.random.RandomState(0)); print(f.summary()['mu'], f.result.acceptance_rate)"   Vector case: attackG_hmc.py last block (DiagGaussian(5, mean=free(5,name='v'), var=0.25).fit(X, how='hmc', constraints=[increasing(v)])). Full comparison vs nuts/ensemble/mcmc and the truncated-normal reference: attackF_parallel_hmc.py.
expected: Samples from the truncated posterior (reference truncated-normal mean 6.009, std 0.009; nuts gives 6.011/0.011, ensemble 6.012/0.012, mcmc 6.010/0.010) or a raised error.
observed: Scalar: {'mean': 6.2353, 'std': 0.0, 'q2.5': 6.2353, 'q97.5': 6.2353, 'ess_bulk': nan, ...}, acceptance_rate 0.0, all 2000 draws identical to the _project_init point; same with chains=2 and with torch absent. Inactive constraints (mu>0, mu<100), penalty= (soft) and potentials sample normally (acc ~0.99). Vector: 'ValueError: grad_log_target returned non-finite values'.
notes: posterior_summary(f) does flag diagnostic_status='unusable', so the release's diagnostics gate catches it if used; .summary() and .posterior() do not. The hmc_fit docstring only says ensemble/mcmc 'usually mixes better' for hard constraints.

title: Every posterior-bearing PPL fit (conjugate, mcmc, hmc, nuts, ensemble, laplace, vi, vmp) is unpicklable; dump_models rejects RandomVariable outright; explain_fit docstring promises the record 'travels with the model through pickling'
surface: pickle.dumps(RandomVariable bound by those fitters); mixle.stats.dump_models; local closures in inference._finalize/_finalize_chains/vi_fit/vmp_fit ('predictive') and _conj_normal_mean (lambda)
reproduction: cd <review-root>/reviews-081/pass-04 && <venv>/bin/python repro_pickle.py ; plus: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Normal, free; from mixle.stats import dump_models; dd=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(5,2,400)); f=Normal(Normal(0,10,name='mu'),free).fit(dd,how='mcmc',draws=50,burn=20,rng=np.random.RandomState(0)); dump_models(f)"
expected: Fitted PPL models round-trip through pickle (per RandomVariable.explain_fit docstring, core.py ~2612) or through a documented mixle serializer, keeping the posterior and the fit record.
observed: map/em/hierarchical fits pickle fine; conjugate -> AttributeError: Can't get local object '_conj_normal_mean.<locals>.<lambda>'; mcmc/hmc/nuts/laplace -> '_finalize.<locals>.predictive'; ensemble -> '_finalize_chains.<locals>.predictive'; vi -> 'vi_fit.<locals>.predictive'; vmp -> 'vmp_fit.<locals>.predictive'. dump_models(rv) -> SerializationError: objects of type mixle.ppl.core.RandomVariable are not JSON serializable by mixle (for every fit kind); dump_models(rv.dist) succeeds but keeps only the point distribution (posterior draws, summary, explanation dropped).
notes: The same closures are why hmc_fit/mcmc_fit/nuts_fit force parallel=False with constraints ('closures do not survive process pickling').

title: potential() docstring says every referenced RV must be a model parameter ('as with constraints'); a foreign RV is silently accepted and integrated as a new latent with its prior
reproduction: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Normal, HalfNormal, potential; dd=list(np.random.RandomState(0).normal(5,2,400)); mu=Normal(0,10,name='mu'); sg=HalfNormal(5,name='sg'); zz=Normal(0,1,name='zz'); print(Normal(mu,sg).fit(dd,how='map',potentials=potential(lambda z: 0.0, zz)).params)"   (a constraint on zz raises 'a constraint references an RV that is not a parameter of this model')
expected: Per docstring: ValueError. Or the docstring documents that a potential may introduce auxiliary latents (which _potential_latents' private docstring says).
observed: Returns {'mean': 4.94, 'sd': 1.98} with no error; zz becomes an extra slot.
notes: Behaviour is defensible; the public contract contradicts it.

title: explain_fit() on a model fitted with how='auto' reports reason "explicit how='map'", losing the pre-fit auto-routing reason
reproduction: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import DiagGaussian, free, increasing; r=np.random.RandomState(0); X=np.stack([r.normal(l,0.5,300) for l in [0,2,1,3,4]],axis=1).tolist(); v=free(5,name='v'); m=DiagGaussian(5,mean=v,var=np.full(5,.25)); print(m.explain_fit(constraints=[increasing(v)])); print(m.fit(X,how='auto',constraints=[increasing(v)]).explain_fit())"
expected: Bound record keeps 'constraints/potentials need the numerical joint -> MAP (a point estimate)' as the reason.
observed: Pre-fit: {'route': 'map', 'reason': 'constraints/potentials need the numerical joint -> MAP (a point estimate)'}; post-fit: {'route': 'map', 'reason': "explicit how='map' (requested how='auto'; resolved to 'map' by fit)", 'route_requested': 'auto'}.
notes: route and route_requested are correct; only the reason text is wrong.

title: Grouped (.each()) constrained MAP reports optimizer.iterations = 0 for the derivative-free path
surface: mixle.ppl.inference.map_fit grouped branch (grouped_nit = 0 hard-coded, inference.py ~2421); IndexedPosterior.summary()['optimizer']
reproduction: python -c "import numpy as np; from mixle.ppl import Normal, free; groups=[list(np.random.RandomState(k).normal(k-2,1.0,30)) for k in range(6)]; m=Normal(0,100,name='m'); th=Normal(m,3.0,name='th').each(); print(Normal(th,free).fit(groups,how='map',constraints=[m>3],rng=np.random.RandomState(0)).summary()['optimizer'])"
expected: A real iteration/evaluation count, or the key omitted.
observed: {'algorithm': 'powell-penalty+nelder-mead', 'success': True, 'iterations': 0, 'message': 'constrained optimum reached', 'objective': 272.35} (the value m=3.000000000000088 itself is correct).
